title: Unit tests for session persistence
description:
Add Zig `test` blocks for `session_persistence.zig`:

- Round-trip: serialize session → deserialize → compare fields match

- Deserialize corrupt JSON → graceful fallback to default state
- Deserialize empty string → default state
- Deserialize JSON with missing fields → defaults filled in (forward compat)
- Deserialize JSON with extra unknown fields → ignored (backward compat)
- Split layout tree serialization: single pane, 2-way split, nested 3-way split
- Workspace list ordering preserved through round-trip

Run with: `zig build test`
acceptance_criteria:
- Round-trip serialization is lossless for all field types
- Corrupt/missing/empty input → fresh state, no crash
- Unknown fields in JSON are tolerated

title: Socket server implementation
description:
Create `src/apprt/gtk/class/socket_server.zig`. Listens on `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/cove/socket` (fallback: `/tmp/cove-$UID/socket`). GLib main loop integration via `g_unix_fd_add()` for accept + read. Newline-delimited JSON protocol (one JSON object per line, response per line). Auth: file-permission based (socket is 0600). Wire into `application.zig`: start server on activate, stop on shutdown.

cmux ref: `SocketControlSettings` in `SocketControlSettings.swift` ~L1–385; socket path from CMUX_SOCKET_PATH env; `CLI/cmux.swift` ~L620–710 client-side connection.
acceptance_criteria:
- Socket file created on launch at correct path with 0600 permissions
- Socket removed on clean shutdown
- Accepts multiple concurrent connections
- Responds to ping with {"ok": true}
- Handles malformed JSON gracefully (returns error, stays functional)
